answer: Postal anchoring: (1) enrollment mails a sealed card to a street address bearing a one-time code and barcode. (2) The recipient enters it within 14 days; the node hashes the address with an epoch salt and keeps only the hash. (3) A second identity claiming that hash is rejected and its card voided. (4) Delivery scans are mirrored publicly, so a spiral of reused mail drops shows as one repeating hash. Renting 5,000 deliverable addresses costs $150,000 monthly at $30 each, plus $4.50 registered post per card. A rented IP is a whisper; a postmarked envelope is a vault door with a witness.
